title: Monthly resource-band changes and job-count changes are distinct adjacent-month pathways
source_unit: identified SIPP person record across adjacent reference months, with explicitly monthly income-to-poverty and job-count fields

observations.period: 2024 reference year; resource band at month t to job-count change at month t+1

denominator.unit: valid adjacent person-month pairs with monthly resource band at t and job count at t+1; resource-band cells retain their own pair universes

below_1x_next_job_count_changes.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.152 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 2.214–2.811

1_to_2x_next_job_count_changes.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.103 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 1.425–1.828

2_to_4x_next_job_count_changes.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.066 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 1.491–1.751

4x_or_more_next_job_count_changes.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.054 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 1.510–1.721

observations.method: Same-person adjacent-month cross-lag using first-month WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights; THINCPOV is classified below 1x, 1–2x, 2–4x, and 4x-or-more monthly income-to-poverty ratio, and RMNUMJOBS change is any category change at the following month.
observations.uncertainty: Fay-BRR intervals quantify design-based sampling uncertainty for the person-record cross-lag. The result is descriptive and does not establish that resource position caused a job-count change.
observations.subgroup: Identified SIPP persons with valid monthly income-to-poverty band at t and valid job counts at t and t+1; cells use separate valid pair universes.
observations.counterinterpretation: The lower-resource group has a somewhat higher next-month job-count-change share, but the comparison may reflect household composition, earnings, transfers, job quality, hours, or selection; job count is not work intensity or income recovery.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; job count at month t to resource-band change at month t+1

denominator.unit: valid adjacent person-month pairs with monthly job count at t and resource band at t+1; job-count cells retain their own pair universes

zero_jobs_next_resource_band_changes.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.100 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 2.792–3.183

one_job_next_resource_band_changes.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.118 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 3.512–3.977

two_jobs_next_resource_band_changes.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.323 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 4.365–5.630

three_jobs_next_resource_band_changes.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 1.209 percentage points; approximate 95% CI 2.807–7.546

observations.method: Same-person adjacent-month cross-lag using first-month WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights; RMNUMJOBS is the number of jobs in month t, and THINCPOV band change is evaluated at t+1.
observations.uncertainty: The smallest high-job-count cells are imprecise; job count and income-to-poverty ratio have different meanings and neither captures hours, pay, care, schedule control, or a specific shock.
observations.subgroup: Identified SIPP persons with valid monthly job count at t and valid income-to-poverty bands at t and t+1.
observations.counterinterpretation: More jobs can coexist with resource-band movement because earnings, household income, transfers, and costs also change; a resource-band change is not necessarily an employment response.

related_sources.claim: Official monthly field definitions and universes for THINCPOV and RMNUMJOBS.
Official 240-replicate-weight archive used for Fay-BRR uncertainty.

boundary: This is a same-person monthly descriptive cross-lag for explicitly monthly SIPP fields. It does not establish causality, household-weighted prevalence, exact bill or care events, hours, pay, schedule control, health, institutional remedy, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence. Annual/reference-period hardship fields are not promoted into this monthly event measure.
